last_frame.description: Optional end pose, same size as first_frame — the motion is generated between the two.

description.title: Description
description.description: The motion to generate (e.g. 'walking forward', 'sword slash', 'flame flickering'). Describe movement, not appearance.

frame_count.title: Frame Count
frame_count.description: Frames to generate, a multiple of 4 from 4 to 40, at any size up to 256x256.

no_background.title: No Background
no_background.description: True returns the frames on transparency; an opaque input is cut out of its first frame before animating. False keeps an opaque backdrop.

drift_threshold.title: Drift Threshold
drift_threshold.description: Color de-flicker sensitivity. Frames whose foreground drifts from the first frame beyond this are corrected toward it; 0 corrects every frame, higher values correct fewer. Omit for the default.

enhance_prompt.title: Enhance Prompt
enhance_prompt.description: If true, rewrite `description` as PixMiniMax's action caption before generating: the motion in playback order with weight, follow-through and recovery, and nothing about appearance, pose, view or facing (those are separate caption fields). Equivalent to calling /v2/enhance-animation-v3-prompt with engine='pixminimax' first. Costs an additional 0.05 generations (or equivalent credits). The expanded text is returned in `enhanced_prompt`.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Facing direction of the sprite (south = towards the camera), the model's facing caption field. Omit to have it read from the image.

view.title: View
view.description: Camera view of the sprite, the model's view caption field. Omit to have it read from the image.

subject_description.title: Subject Description
subject_description.description: What first_frame shows, one noun phrase (e.g. 'a knight in silver plate armour'), the model's subject caption field. Omit to have it read from the image.

initial_pose.title: Initial Pose
initial_pose.description: The pose first_frame is in (e.g. 'standing upright with the sword lowered'), the model's starting-pose caption field. Omit to have it read from the image.

AnimatePixminimaxRequest.title: AnimatePixminimaxRequest
AnimatePixminimaxRequest.description: Request model for the PixMiniMax animation endpoint (powered by MiniMax H3)

description.title: Description
description.description: Description of what to generate in the masked area

mask_image.description: Mask for the image (same dimensions as inpainting_image). White = generate, Black = preserve

crop_to_mask.title: Crop To Mask
crop_to_mask.description: Whether to crop generated content to mask boundary (ensures clean edges)

first_frame.description: First frame to animate (PNG/JPEG base64, max 256x256 pixels)

last_frame.description: Optional last frame to guide the animation endpoint (PNG/JPEG base64, max 256x256 pixels)

frame_count.title: Frame Count
frame_count.description: Number of animation frames (4-16, must be even)

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Seed for reproducible generation (0 for random)

drift_threshold.title: Drift Threshold
drift_threshold.description: Color de-flicker sensitivity. Frames whose foreground drifts from the first frame beyond this are corrected toward it; 0 corrects every frame, higher values correct fewer. Omit for the default.

enhance_prompt.title: Enhance Prompt
enhance_prompt.description: If true, automatically expand `action` into a richer motion description before generating — equivalent to calling /v2/enhance-animation-v3-prompt with these frames first. Uses `first_frame` (and `last_frame` for interpolation) to ground the description. Costs an additional 0.05 generations (or equivalent credits). The expanded text is returned in `enhanced_prompt`.

AnimateWithTextV3Request.title: AnimateWithTextV3Request
AnimateWithTextV3Request.description: Request model for animate with text v3 endpoint

target_palette.description: Colours the result must use and/or a colour cap: {"colors": ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"], "name": "Game Boy", "max_colors": 4}. With colors every pixel of every frame (one choice for all frames) is one of them; max_colors (2-64) caps the colours of every frame (one choice for all frames).
